site: Imagined corner of John’s Cornish home garden. John has no fruit cage on site. The illustrated cage, positions, planting and summer scene are fictional. Do not use these pictures as site survey or camera evidence.

online_research.detail: Customer-built setting and installed timber-cage photographs, including the Wiltshire example. Used for real scale and the way light passes through the enclosure.
Walk-in proportions, timber uprights and roof supports, door and separately fitted lighter roof net. Harrod describes extruded side netting; the book specifies galvanised wire.

Maker’s Tunstall case study documents galvanised square wire fixed to timber and a fitted gate and latch. Used for side materials and access. The formal towers and ornamental gates are specific to that commission.

generation.prompt:
Make ONE horizontal 4:3 photorealistic British gardening-book photograph titled in concept A PERMANENT FRUIT CAGE, but do not put any text on the image. Show a workmanlike, walk-in DIY timber fruit cage in a fictional corner of the gardener’s own Cornish HOME garden, in soft, bright early-summer daylight. First input is a real photo of his winter fruit border: loosely adapt the camera direction, the low weathered grey block boundary and short strip of faded timber lattice, dark soil and small domestic proportions, but IMAGINE a modest extra corner with room for the cage and a grassy approach, in summer with some leaves. Second input is the book’s existing graphic construction reference ONLY: the new result must be a natural colour photograph with a real garden background, not a rendering, outline, miniature, pristine wood product photo, or cream vignette. Third input shows his real summers' foliage and ordinary materials for atmosphere; keep its hen house and shed outside this composition. No gardener needed.
Make the instructional subject legible within a 70 mm wide book picture. A simple freestanding elongated rectangular enclosure of human standing height, a plausible roughly 2 m tall, 2.7 m wide and 3.6 m deep by eye. Show the entire frame from the grass at its foot to the roof, with a modest breathing margin on all four sides, filling about 82–87 percent of image width. Three-quarter view from the approach, showing the door on one end and the longer adjacent side, with just enough of the top plane visible to read the closed roof. Keep the eye level just above the top of the frame if necessary and the perspective natural. Sturdy, grey honey-brown weathered square-section timber posts driven into soil, joined by simple top rails and short timber corner knee braces. One intermediate post on each long side, with a cross support for the bird net at roof level. The sides and framed door are skinned with taut fine silver-grey galvanised welded square WIRE mesh, securely fixed to the perimeter and reaching down to the ground. Its delicate open grid is visible where light catches it, but transparent enough to see actual fruit bushes. A separate flat dark, lightweight BIRD NET covers the entire roof, visibly distinct from the wire sides, properly stretched and neatly secured along all edges, no loose tails or holes. NO solid roof panels or diagonal roof decking; a light roof which still lets the sky and foliage show through. The entry is an unambiguous single adult-sized, CLOSED rectangular timber-and-wire gate neatly fitted between two posts, small galvanised strap hinges on one side, an ordinary latch on the opposite side, modest diagonal timber brace from the lower hinge corner towards the upper latch corner. A clear, inviting wood-chip picking path leads up to the gate and continues in the same direction BETWEEN the planting inside: the entrance is usable, door and path not blocked by bushes. Inside are a few established British soft-fruit bushes of visibly different heights, widths and leaf silhouettes; a few small dangling strings of redcurrants among lobed leaves in the nearer bed cue their purpose, a looser upright bush further back, modestly visible patches of berry colour. Enough space between bushes, mesh, and walking route for a gardener to pick and prune. Ordinary timber grain, slightly uneven mown grass, useable garden with a handful of small imperfections. Subordinate simple background: a little familiar grey masonry and timber lattice, dark irregular green foliage near the top, no structure competing with the cage. Natural British garden photography, restrained colour, real scale. No animals, no humans, no signage, captions or inset, no other cages or poultry runs.

references_in_order.use: Camera direction, low block wall and lattice at John’s fruit border. Centred 4:3 crop enlarged to 1448 × 1086 for the reference.
Teaching reference for the construction, gate, bracing, wire sides, net roof and picking aisle.
John’s home garden in leaf. Foliage and domestic scale only.
